currentContext.business: Shiva Cement, incorporated in Odisha in 1985 and a subsidiary of JSW Cement Limited (part of the JSW Group) since 2017, manufactures clinker and, from FY 2025-26, cement. Its manufacturing set-up comprises a clinkerisation plant, a cement grinding unit, a waste heat recovery power plant and captive limestone mines, with the clinker plant acting as a feeder to JSW Cement's eastern plants. The commissioning and ramp-up of a 1 MTPA grinding unit at Sambalpur enabled the transition from a pure clinker manufacturer to an integrated cement producer serving eastern Indian markets through JSW Cement's distribution network.

Cement: CHD Jalkavach (premium offering marketed by parent JSW Cement)

Waste Heat Recovery System (WHRS) meeting approximately 60% of the clinker plant's power requirement

Dedicated railway siding for inward/outward movement, commissioned in 2026

currentContext.expansion: FY 2025-26 was the year Shiva Cement's multi-year investment cycle in clinker capacity expansion, infrastructure and downstream integration began to convert into operating outcomes. The landmark project of the year was the 1 MTPA cement grinding unit at Sambalpur, Odisha, commissioned on September 03, 2025 under an exclusive manufacturing partnership with group company Bhushan Power and Steel Limited (BPSL); its commissioning and ramp-up moved the Company from pure clinker manufacturing to integrated cement production alongside the existing 4,000 TPD (1.32 MTPA) clinkerisation plant that had commenced commercial operation in June 2023. The Company also commissioned a dedicated railway siding at Sagra for inward and outward movement in 2026. On the supply-chain side, limestone sourcing was increased from both existing and auctioned mines and significant progress was made on pre-project activities for a belt conveyor system to move limestone from the mines to the plant, a project management intends to complete and commission in FY 2026-27 and expects to lower logistics costs and carbon emissions. Under JSW Group's guidance the Company states it is poised to expand clinker capacity further and to introduce cement blends such as Portland Composite Cement (PCC). With major expansion projects substantially completed, FY 2026-27 priorities shift from project execution to value creation - maximising grinding-unit utilisation, expanding value-added products and commercialising dolomite sales. The MD&A notes that debt increased due to availment of a fresh term loan for project activity.

risks.note: The MD&A's risk table states the cement sector is prone to supply-demand mismatches and faces fluctuations in its end-user sectors; with the industry adding roughly 50-55 MTPA of capacity in FY 2025-26 and a further 42-44 MTPA planned for FY 2026-27, regional oversupply can compress realisations for a small eastern-India producer.

Management flags that production is constrained by difficulties in sourcing sufficient, suitable-quality limestone; the Company mitigates through captive mines, auctioned mines, strategic inventory and specialist consultants for limestone deposit utilisation plans, but limestone availability is also cited industry-wide as a constraint on capacity addition.

risks.risk: Input and energy cost volatility (coal, pet coke, fuel)
risks.note: The stated raw-material risk is continual margin erosion from volatile input costs, with rising global prices for coal and pet coke directly increasing manufacturing expenditure. Geopolitical tension in West Asia raised crude, pet coke, imported coal and diesel costs during the year; management says these pressures intensified late in FY 2025-26 and are expected to persist in the near term.

The Company states the cement industry is highly exposed to logistical inefficiencies, with higher freight costs and inadequate critical infrastructure, particularly rail freight capacity and last-mile connectivity. Mitigation rests on the newly commissioned Sagra railway siding and the planned limestone belt conveyor, both still to prove savings.

The MD&A ratio commentary notes debt increased due to availment of a fresh term loan for project activity together with equity erosion, resulting in negative net worth for the year, and flags a DBS Bank term loan bullet payment of Rs 201.50 Cr due in March 2027 - a concentrated refinancing/repayment event against a loss-making year and rising finance cost.

risks.risk: Dependence on the JSW group for offtake, distribution and operations
risks.note: The clinker plant is described as a key feeder to the Group's eastern plants; market presence is built on JSW Cement's established distribution network, the premium product is marketed by the parent as CHD Jalkavach, the 1 MTPA grinding capacity runs under an exclusive manufacturing partnership with group company Bhushan Power & Steel Limited, and CSR spending is borne by the holding company. Commercial terms and volumes are therefore substantially group-determined; the MD&A also notes there are no trade receivables as all sales are made against advance.

Operations sit at one plant site at Village Telighana, Kutra, District Sundargarh, Odisha, with mines at Village Khatkurbahal, serving Odisha, West Bengal, Jharkhand and Bihar - so any disruption at the site, its mines or in eastern-India demand hits the entire business, and the new capacity is a single grinding unit at Sambalpur.

risks.risk: Execution and ramp-up of the new capacity
risks.note: FY 2026-27 earnings depend on maximising utilisation of the just-commissioned 1 MTPA grinding unit and on completing the belt conveyor project, which was still at pre-project activity stage; jobwork charges for operating the BPSL grinding unit already drove other expenses up 81.88%, so ramp shortfalls would leave the added cost without the volume.

The Company's own EHS risk entry states that growing environmental concerns and regulatory requirements on greenhouse gas emissions could limit its operations, and that the industry faces strict labour laws and health and safety regulations. Cement is among the most energy-intensive and carbon-emitting industrial processes, and the Company's Thermal Substitution Rate moderated during FY 2025-26 versus the prior year, leaving its alternative-fuel progress a live watch item.
